extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners building/evaluating creative-writing datasets; expert annotators and NLP/ML researchers using human/LLM evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric and set of diagnostic tests (TTCW) for assessing short literary stories on dimensions like originality, fluency, rhetorical complexity, character/world-building, and flexibility; intended for expert annotators and LLM evaluation. Provides binary/diagnostic questions plus expanded guidance for each measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive techniques like time jumping, varied perspectives, unconventional punctuation, and delayed revelation of key information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing stories use inventive formal techniques that contribute to the story’s originality; failing stories are conventional and linear in form, language, and narrative, with occasional attempts at innovation that do not significantly contribute to overall creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Fresh language, unique plot and characters, subtle emotional resonance, and inventive metaphors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing: language and metaphors feel fresh and imaginative; failing: story relies heavily on clichés and tired tropes, language feels predictable, and the narrative arc follows familiar trajectories lacking novelty or nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Theme/Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unconventional, dreamlike exploration of emotions (e.g., love and loss) that evoke empathy and reflection through a distinct character perspective and ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing: eschews simplistic meanings for ambiguity and open-ended questions; failing: disjointed narrative, underdeveloped themes, inconsistent tone, vaguely defined characters, abrupt context shifts, lacking depth and substantive insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: World Building and Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic use of concrete, specific sensory details from a particular character’s perspective to make a fictional world feel real, vivid and immersive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing: thoughtful depiction of everyday objects and idiosyncratic elements, balancing exposition with vivid scene-setting to create authenticity that serves plot and characters. Failing: world not convincingly established through sensory detail; overreliance on overwrought imagery and figurative language without grounding the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully realized characters with contradictions, motivations, and backstories that make them feel lifelike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing: characters have depth and nuance appropriate to narrative goals. Failing: flat or stereotypical characters, predictable arcs, unclear motivations leading to reader disconnect; note that less-developed characters may be acceptable if stylistically intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rich subtext emerging through contrasts between characters and settings, omissions that let readers fill in meaning, layered metaphors, implicit characterization, ambiguous endings, and intertextual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing: language and structure invite multiple interpretations and subtlety; failing: straightforward storytelling, lack of nuance/ambiguity, overtelling instead of showing, expository dialogue, blunt symbolism, and definitive endings that limit interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Pacing (Compression/Stretching of Time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manipulation of time in terms of compression or stretching feel appropriate and balanced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: compression condenses long spans into summary; stretching slows brief moments for emphasis. Evaluate relation between story-time and real-world reading time and whether compression/stretching serves dramatic effect without undermining engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene vs Summary/Exposition (Balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story have an appropriate balance between scene (dramatised, real-time moments) and summary/exposition (condensed events or background)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: scenes are vivid, featuring dialogue/action; summaries move the story forward or provide background. Too many scenes may overwhelm or slow pace; too much exposition can feel dry and unengaging. Assess whether balance maintains pace and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Proficiency & Literary Devices (Idiom/Metaphor/Allusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story make sophisticated use of idiom, metaphor, or literary allusion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: idiom lends authenticity to voice; metaphors create original comparisons revealing insight; allusions add contextual richness. Evaluation asks annotators/LLMs to list metaphors/idioms/allusions, judge whether each is successful or forced, and then answer overall Yes/No.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Ending (Earned Conclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the end of the story feel natural and earned, as opposed to arbitrary or abrupt?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: an earned ending ties up central conflicts or reaches the moment the piece has been building toward. Abrupt or 'writer-tired' endings suggest rushed conclusions; assess whether resolution provides closure and feels purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandability & Coherence (Unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the different elements of the story work together to form a unified, engaging, and satisfying whole?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: evaluate whether beginning sets up middle and end logically, and whether scenes, character actions, and dialogue serve and propel the story. Disorder or disconnection indicates failing coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective & Voice Flexibility (Diverse Perspectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story provide diverse perspectives, and if there are unlikeable characters, are their perspectives presented convincingly and accurately?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: assess the writer’s ability to depict a range of viewpoints, including morally ambiguous or objectionable perspectives, by conveying believable motivations and inner logic without endorsing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Flexibility (Interiority vs Exteriority Balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story achieve a good balance between interiority (characters' thoughts/feelings) and exteriority (observable actions/behavior), yielding emotional flexibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: a balance prevents stories from being overly introspective (losing momentum) or overly external (lacking depth). Evaluate whether the piece portrays a broad, realistic spectrum of emotions and balances action with introspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising-but-Appropriate Turns
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story contain turns that are both surprising and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded guidance: 'surprising' = unpredictable developments; 'appropriate' = coherent in hindsight and consistent with established rules/characterization. Annotators list surprising elements and judge whether each is fitting within the story’s universe and character logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of Voice & Diction (Suggested Additional Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency in voice and diction across the story as a measurable test (recommended by experts as potentially crucial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes from experts: some felt the rubric overlooked voice, noting inconsistent voice/diction often marks weaker stories and that voice conveys artistry, personality, and identity. Suggested addition for future rubric iterations to measure this explicitly.
